titleEn: Cardiac Chest Pain - ASA and Nitroglycerin

patient.name: Robert Hale
patient.affectEn: anxious and frightened; grey and diaphoretic; sitting on the edge of the bed with one fist clenched over the middle of his sternum (Levine sign); does not want to move
patient.speechEn: speaks in short sentences because of the pain; cooperative, answers every question but does not volunteer information that is not asked for

scene.settingEn: Upstairs bedroom of a townhouse in Coquitlam at 0640 hrs. Warm, well-lit room. The only way in or out is the staircase you climbed: 14 steps with a narrow turn. No pets, no smoking materials, no other hazards. One patient.
hazardsEn: stair egress: 14 narrow steps with a tight turn, the only way out

bystanders.knowsEn: He woke at 0615 with chest pain and has been sweating since. He has not taken anything for it. There is no nitroglycerin in the house; he has never had heart trouble before. She called 911 and waited at the door for you. She can fetch his pill bottles from the kitchen if asked.

scene.partnerEn: one partner at your licence level; acts only on your delegation
equipmentEn: oxygen kit with non-rebreather mask and nasal cannula
cot (stretcher) left at the bottom of the stairs
PCP only: IV start kit with normal saline, dimenhydrinate

dispatchEn: 0640 hrs. Code 3 to a townhouse complex in Coquitlam. 62-year-old male with central chest pain that woke him from sleep. His wife made the call. Hospital with a cath lab is 14 minutes away.
dispatchUpdateEn: Dispatch adds: he is conscious, sweating, and has not taken anything for the pain. No prescribed nitroglycerin in the house.
arrivalEn: Wife meets you at the front door, visibly worried, and leads you up the stairs to the bedroom. The room is warm and well lit. The staircase you just climbed is the only way back down: 14 steps with a narrow turn. Your partner is right behind you with the kits. One patient. No pets, no smoking materials, no other hazards.
firstLookEn: A 62-year-old man sitting on the edge of the bed, grey and diaphoretic, one fist clenched over the middle of his sternum. He looks up at you and speaks in short sentences: "It feels like a weight on my chest."

primary.locEn: Alert. Oriented to person, place, time and event. Answers in short sentences because of the pain.
primary.airwayEn: Open and clear. Speaking in short sentences, no abnormal sounds, no secretions.
primary.breathingEn: Rate 22, slightly laboured, adequate depth, equal chest rise, no wheeze.
primary.circulationEn: Radial pulse 96, regular, normal strength. No external bleeding.
primary.rbsEn: Modified rapid body survey for a medical patient: no trauma, no edema, no obvious abnormality; abdomen soft. Skin pale, cool, diaphoretic (skin is given automatically with the RBS).

history.ccEn: It's my chest. Right in the middle. It feels like a weight sitting on it.

opqrst.oEn: I was asleep. It woke me up at about a quarter past six. I wasn't doing anything, I was in bed.
opqrst.pEn: Nothing makes it better. I tried sitting up, I tried lying back down. Taking a deep breath doesn't change it either.
opqrst.qEn: Heavy. Like a pressure, like a band pulled tight around my chest.
opqrst.rEn: It goes up into my left jaw and down my left arm. Nothing has given me any relief. I had two milder ones like this earlier this week when I was exerting myself, but those went away once I sat down and rested.
opqrst.tEn: It's been constant since it woke me, about 25 minutes now. It hasn't let up at all.

sample.sEn: The chest pressure, I feel sick to my stomach, I'm sweating, and I'm a bit short of breath.
sample.aEn: No allergies that I know of. Not to aspirin, not to anything.
sample.mEn: Amlodipine 5 milligrams for my blood pressure and rosuvastatin 10 milligrams for cholesterol. That's all I take. (Only if specifically asked about Viagra, Levitra, Cialis or erectile dysfunction medication: "No. None of those. Never have." Only if asked about nitro at home: "No, I've never been given any.")
sample.pEn: High blood pressure and high cholesterol, both on pills. I quit smoking 3 years ago; before that it was about a pack a day for 30 years. My father died of a heart attack at 58. I've never had heart trouble myself before this week. No diabetes.
sample.lEn: Dinner at 1900 last night, about 7 o'clock. Nothing since.
sample.eEn: Nothing. I was asleep. It just woke me up. No exertion, no argument, no fall.

fe.generalEn: I've been well, fit for my age, until this week. No fevers, no weight loss, no change in energy before this.
fe.cnsEn: No fainting, no blackouts, no headache. No weakness or numbness anywhere.
fe.respiratoryEn: I'm a bit short of breath with the pain. No cough. I don't need extra pillows to sleep and I don't wake up breathless.
fe.cardiovascularEn: This pressure that goes into my jaw and arm. No palpitations, no racing heart. No swollen ankles. Two milder episodes this week when I was exerting myself; both settled with rest.
fe.giGuEn: I feel nauseated but I haven't thrown up. It's not heartburn and it's not like indigestion. Bowels and waterworks are normal.
fe.integumentaryEn: I'm sweating heavily. No rash, no bruising, no sores.
fe.musculoskeletalEn: I haven't hurt my chest. No fall, no lifting, no strain. It doesn't hurt any more when you press on it.
fe.eentEn: Nothing. Eyes, ears, nose and throat are all fine.

findings.headNeckEn: No JVD. Trachea midline. Nothing else of note.
findings.chestLungsEn: No chest wall tenderness; the pain is NOT reproducible on palpation. Air entry equal and clear in all 6 sites, no crackles, no wheeze. Equal chest rise.
findings.abdomenEn: Soft, non-tender in all quadrants. No distension.
findings.backEn: No findings: no tenderness, no deformity.
findings.lowerExtremitiesEn: No pedal edema. Pedal pulses present and equal bilaterally. Normal colour, movement and sensation.
findings.upperExtremitiesEn: Radial pulses equal bilaterally. No motor or sensory deficit; grip strength equal.

vitalsSets.unlockNoteEn: after 2 doses of nitroglycerin, en route; pain down from 8/10 to 3/10; systolic still above 110 so a third dose is permitted if pain persists

stateChanges.examinerLineEn: The patient tells you he feels light-headed and washed out. When a blood pressure is next taken it is 96/60, systolic now below 110: the next nitroglycerin dose must be withheld and the Entonox pathway considered 5 minutes after the last dose.

triggers: I'll bring the cot and the stair chair up to the patient
I'm planning for a cardiac call
bring everything up so he does not have to walk

expected.actionEn: Anticipate a time-critical cardiac call and plan early transport with hospital notification
triggers: we will want to be moving early

expected.actionEn: Verbalize hazards (stair egress), environment, nature of illness (chest pain), number of patients (1)
triggers: nature of illness is chest pain
the stairs are our egress problem
environment is warm and well lit

expected.actionEn: Don gloves and eye protection
triggers: I'm putting on gloves and eye protection

expected.actionEn: First look: grey, diaphoretic, clenched fist over sternum (Levine sign)
Plan the stair egress early and bring equipment to the patient rather than walking him
triggers: partner, set up the stair chair
stair chair ready at the top

expected.actionEn: Assess LOC / AVPU: Alert
triggers: do you know where you are

expected.actionEn: Verbalize c-spine not indicated (medical presentation)
Assess airway
triggers: he's talking so his airway is clear

expected.actionEn: Assess breathing rate, depth and effort
Assess radial pulse rate, strength and regularity
Perform a modified rapid body survey appropriate to a medical patient
Note skin: pale cool diaphoretic

expected.actionEn: Titrate oxygen only to maintain SpO2 at or above 94% - at 96% RA supplemental oxygen is not required; verbalize the decision
triggers: SpO2 is 96 so no oxygen needed

expected.actionEn: Keep at rest in a position of comfort; limit all patient movement and exertion
Administer ASA 160 mg chewed and swallowed after the rapid body survey (ASA is the one drug not requiring vitals first)
Categorize as RTC and act with urgency
Ready to load within 15 minutes; carry the patient down the stairs, do not let him walk
Delegate the partner to prep egress and the stair chair while you run the protocol
triggers: set up the stair chair while I give the nitro
partner, get the cot ready at the bottom

Full OPQRRRST pain assessment including radiation, recurrence and severity

anything make it better or worse

expected.actionEn: Obtain a 0-10 pain score
PMHx with cardiac risk factors and time scales

Allergies incl aspirin sensitivity before giving ASA
LOI
GCS with components

FE - Respiratory (orthopnea, cough)

Back exam
Lower extremities incl pedal edema and pulses
Upper extremities incl bilateral pulse comparison
Initiate the Cardiac Chest Pain protocol with correct indications and sequence (ASA after RBS, nitroglycerin after baseline vitals)
triggers: ASA after the RBS, nitro after vitals

expected.actionEn: ASA 160 mg PO chewed with 6 rights; rule out allergy, active GI bleed/peptic ulcer, inability to swallow, prior dose taken
triggers: right patient right drug right dose
have you taken any aspirin today

expected.actionEn: Nitroglycerin 0.4 mg SL with contraindications ruled out (SBP under 110, HR under 50 or over 150, nitrate allergy, PDE5 inhibitor use) and vitals repeated before each dose
Verbalize the maximum of 3 nitroglycerin doses in 30 minutes and the Entonox rule (5 minutes after the last nitroglycerin dose)
triggers: Entonox 5 minutes after the last nitro
no Entonox within 5 minutes of nitro

expected.actionEn: PCP: vascular access with running fluid; consider dimenhydrinate for nausea
Reassess ABCs and all interventions after each dose and each move
Full second set of vitals within 5-6 minutes and before the next nitroglycerin dose
triggers: recheck BP before the next dose

expected.actionEn: Reassess the pain score after each dose and titrate to pain-free
triggers: where's the pain now out of 10

expected.actionEn: Withhold nitroglycerin if systolic falls below 110 and switch to the Entonox pathway
triggers: systolic is below 110 so I'm holding the nitro

expected.actionEn: En-route notification of a possible acute coronary syndrome
Complete hand-off with ASA and nitroglycerin times, doses and BP trend
Accurate PCR within 5 minutes

specialEvents.descriptionEn: candidate lets the patient stand and walk, walk to the stairs, or walk down the stairs to the ambulance (any self-exertion)
candidate gives a nitroglycerin dose without taking a blood pressure in the minutes immediately before that dose
candidate asks about Viagra, Levitra, Cialis or erectile dysfunction medication (PDE5 inhibitor screen) before nitroglycerin
candidate gives nitroglycerin after a blood pressure with systolic below 110 has been reported (e.g. 96/60)
candidate administers nitroglycerin spray without verbalizing priming the spray, or shakes the container
candidate applies high-flow oxygen by non-rebreather while SpO2 is 96% on room air without a titration rationale
candidate gives Entonox less than 5 minutes after the last nitroglycerin dose

drugs.doseEn: 160 mg PO, chewed and swallowed, single dose after the RBS; the only medication that does not need vitals first
0.4 mg SL spray, repeat every 3-5 minutes while systolic BP stays above 110 and pain persists, maximum 3 doses in any 30-minute period; vitals before every dose; do not shake, verbalize priming
self-administered by inhalation; only 5 minutes or more after the last nitroglycerin dose, when pain persists beyond 3 doses or systolic falls below 110
1 mg/kg to a maximum of 50 mg, IV diluted and given slowly or IM, for nausea

notificationFacts.cc: central chest pressure, suspected acute coronary syndrome / possible STEMI
notificationFacts.hxcc: woke from sleep at 0615 with heavy band-like central chest pressure 8/10 radiating to the left jaw and left arm, with nausea and diaphoresis; two milder exertional episodes earlier this week
notificationFacts.vitals: GCS 15, BP 148/92, pulse 96 regular, resp 22, SpO2 96% on room air; latest BP 122/78, pulse 88, resp 18, SpO2 97%, pain now 3/10
notificationFacts.treatments: kept at rest and carried out; ASA 160 mg chewed; nitroglycerin 0.4 mg SL x2 with BP rechecked before each dose; PCP: IV en route; ETA 14 minutes
notificationFacts.findings: Levine sign, pale cool diaphoretic; no JVD, chest clear, pain not reproducible on palpation; no pedal edema

handoffFacts.cc: central chest pressure that woke him from sleep
handoffFacts.hxcc: onset 0615 at rest (woke him), about 45 minutes of pain by hand-off; heavy band-like pressure radiating to the left jaw and left arm; 8/10 at onset; associated nausea, diaphoresis and shortness of breath; not reproducible on palpation; two milder exertional episodes earlier this week relieved by rest
handoffFacts.initialVitals: GCS 15 (E4 V5 M6), BP 148/92, pulse 96 regular normal strength, resp 22 slightly laboured, skin pale cool diaphoretic, pupils equal and reactive, SpO2 96% on room air
handoffFacts.finalVitals: GCS 15, BP 122/78, pulse 88 regular, resp 18, skin pink warm drying, pupils equal and reactive, SpO2 97% on room air, pain 3/10
handoffFacts.pmhx: hypertension, dyslipidemia, ex-smoker (quit 3 years ago, 30 pack-years), father died of an MI at 58
handoffFacts.meds: amlodipine 5 mg, rosuvastatin 10 mg; no Viagra, Levitra or Cialis (no PDE5 inhibitors)
handoffFacts.allergies: no known allergies; no aspirin sensitivity
handoffFacts.treatments: kept at rest and carried down the stairs; oxygen not required (SpO2 96%); ASA 160 mg PO chewed at 0652; nitroglycerin 0.4 mg SL at 0658 and 0703 with BP rechecked before each dose; RTC transport with cath-lab notification; PCP: IV with running fluid en route
handoffFacts.findings: Levine sign; no JVD, trachea midline; chest clear in all 6 sites, pain not reproducible on palpation; abdomen soft; no pedal edema; pulses equal bilaterally

pcrFacts.cc: Central chest pressure at rest, radiating to left jaw and arm
pcrFacts.hxcc: Woke from sleep 0615; heavy band-like pressure 8/10; radiates left jaw/arm; nausea and diaphoresis; two exertional episodes earlier in the week; not reproducible on palpation
pcrFacts.pmhx: Hypertension, dyslipidemia, ex-smoker 30 pack-years, family history of MI
pcrFacts.meds: Amlodipine 5 mg, rosuvastatin 10 mg; no PDE5 inhibitors
treatments: Rest, position of comfort, carried down stairs
O2 titrated to keep SpO2 94% or above (none required at 96%)
Nitroglycerin 0.4 mg SL at 0658 and 0703, BP rechecked before each
findings: BP 148/92 down to 122/78, pain 8/10 down to 3/10
No JVD, chest clear, no reproducible chest wall pain

trackNotes.emrEn: EMR gives ASA 160 mg PO and nitroglycerin 0.4 mg SL under the same protocol (no physician order required), plus oxygen titration, rest, and rapid transport. EMR does not establish IV access or give dimenhydrinate. Entonox is available at both levels for the post-3-dose pathway. No Functional Enquiry.
trackNotes.pcpEn: PCP adds vascular access with running fluid, dimenhydrinate 1 mg/kg to a maximum of 50 mg for nausea, and the 9-system Functional Enquiry en route. Everything else is identical.

sourcePages: Scenario md-02 (data/practical/scenarios.json): dispatch, scene, primary, transport, history, vitals sets 1-2, FE, exam, interventions, ongoing (BP 96/60 if no recheck before dosing), handoff. BC Provincial Examination Guidelines (current to June 15, 2026): p.7 Findings in Unstable Adult Patients (suspected cardiac chest pain = unstable); p.47 Cardiac Chest Pain protocol (position of comfort and limit movement, oxygen to SpO2 >= 94%, ASA chewed, transport / delegate egress prep, history and baseline vitals, nitroglycerin, PCP IV and dimenhydrinate, Entonox 5 minutes after the last nitroglycerin dose, 3-dose / 30-minute limit, SBP < 110 pathway); p.60 Aspirin (160 mg PO, after the RBS, the only medication not requiring vitals, contraindications); p.63 Dimenhydrinate (1 mg/kg to a maximum of 50 mg); p.65 Entonox (contraindication: nitroglycerin used in the last 5 minutes); p.73 Nitroglycerin (contraindications SBP < 110, HR < 50 or > 150, Viagra/Levitra in 24 h or Cialis in 48 h; 0.4 mg SL q 3-5 min; maximum 3 doses in any 30-minute period; do not shake the spray).
